audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 22, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness, prophetic, and military-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for war alliance, prophetic consensus pressure, Micaiah's sarcasm, lying-spirit vision, assault and imprisonment of dissent, battlefield disguise, targeted killing, random arrow, prolonged dying, blood and dogs, ivory palace, Jehoshaphat's reforms, qadesh translation, maritime extraction, and Ahaziah's succession.

verses.restored: They lived three years without war between Aram and Israel.

familiar.text: And they continued three years without war between Syria and Israel.

modern.text: Then three years passed without war between Aram and Israel.

original.text: וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים אֵ֚ין מִלְחָמָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין אֲרָ֖ם וּבֵ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: In third year Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to king of Israel.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the third year, that Jehoshaphat the king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.

modern.text: However, in the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to visit the king of Israel,

original.text: וַיְהִ֖י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑ית וַיֵּ֛רֶד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: King of Israel said to his servants, Do you know Ramoth-gilead is ours, yet we remain still from taking it from hand of king of Aram?

familiar.text: And the king of Israel said unto his servants, Know ye that Ramoth in Gilead is ours, and we be still, and take it not out of the hand of the king of Syria?

modern.text: who said to his servants, “Do you not know that Ramoth-gilead is ours, but we have failed to take it from the hand of the king of Aram?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל עֲבָדָ֔יו הַיְדַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי לָ֖נוּ רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ מַחְשִׁ֔ים מִקַּ֣חַת אֹתָ֔הּ מִיַּ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אֲרָֽם

verses.restored: He said to Jehoshaphat, Will you go with me to battle at Ramoth-gilead? Jehoshaphat said to king of Israel, I am as you, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.

familiar.text: And he said unto Jehoshaphat, Wilt thou go with me to battle to Ramothgilead? And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses.

modern.text: So he asked Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to fight against Ramoth-gilead?” Jehoshaphat answered the king of Israel, “I am like you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט הֲתֵלֵ֥ךְ אִתִּ֛י לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כָּמ֧וֹנִי כָמ֛וֹךָ כְּעַמִּ֥י כְעַמֶּ֖ךָ כְּסוּסַ֥י כְּסוּסֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Jehoshaphat said to king of Israel, Please inquire this day for word of YHWH.

familiar.text: And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of the LORD to day.

modern.text: But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for the word of the LORD.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל דְּרָשׁ נָ֥א כַיּ֖וֹם אֶת דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: King of Israel gathered prophets, about four hundred men, and said, Shall I go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or refrain? They said, Go up, and Lord will give it into hand of king.

familiar.text: Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said unto them, Shall I go against Ramothgilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for the LORD shall deliver it into the hand of the king.

modern.text: So the king of Israel assembled the prophets, about four hundred men, and asked them, “Should I go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should I refrain?” “Go up,” they replied, “and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king.”

original.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֨ץ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֶֽת הַנְּבִיאִים֮ כְּאַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֣וֹת אִישׁ֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם הַאֵלֵ֞ךְ עַל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם אֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ עֲלֵ֔ה וְיִתֵּ֥ן אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Jehoshaphat said, Is there not still a prophet of YHWH here, that we may inquire from him?

familiar.text: And Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the LORD besides, that we might enquire of him?

modern.text: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here of whom we can inquire?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט הַאֵ֨ין פֹּ֥ה נָבִ֛יא לַיהוָ֖ה ע֑וֹד וְנִדְרְשָׁ֖ה מֵאוֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: King of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, There is still one man through whom to inquire of YHWH, Micaiah son of Imlah, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good concerning me, only evil. Jehoshaphat said, Let king not say so.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, by whom we may enquire of the LORD: but I hate him; for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.

modern.text: The king of Israel answered, “There is still one man who can ask the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” “The king should not say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אֶֽל יְהוֹשָׁפָ֡ט ע֣וֹד אִישׁ אֶחָ֡ד לִדְרֹשׁ֩ אֶת יְהוָ֨ה מֵאֹת֜וֹ וַאֲנִ֣י שְׂנֵאתִ֗יו כִּ֠י לֹֽא יִתְנַבֵּ֨א עָלַ֥י טוֹב֙ כִּ֣י אִם רָ֔ע מִיכָ֖יְהוּ בֶּן יִמְלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט אַל יֹאמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כֵּֽן

verses.restored: King of Israel called an official and said, Hurry Micaiah son of Imlah.

familiar.text: Then the king of Israel called an officer, and said, Hasten hither Micaiah the son of Imlah.

modern.text: So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל סָרִ֖יס אֶחָ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַהֲרָ֖ה מִיכָ֥יְהוּ בֶן יִמְלָֽה

verses.restored: King of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat each upon his throne, clothed in robes, at threshing floor/open place at entrance of gate of Samaria, and all prophets prophesied before them.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah sat each on his throne, having put on their robes, in a void place in the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.

modern.text: Dressed in royal attire, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.

original.text: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֡ה יֹשְׁבִים֩ אִ֨ישׁ עַל כִּסְא֜וֹ מְלֻבָּשִׁ֤ים בְּגָדִים֙ בְּגֹ֔רֶן פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וְכָ֨ל הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made for himself horns of iron and said, Thus says YHWH: With these you shall gore Aram until you finish it.

familiar.text: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made him horns of iron: and he said, Thus saith the LORD, With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until thou have consumed them.

modern.text: Now Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made for himself iron horns and declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are finished off.’”

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥ה בֶֽן כְּנַעֲנָ֖ה קַרְנֵ֣י בַרְזֶ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵ֛לֶּה תְּנַגַּ֥ח אֶת אֲרָ֖ם עַד כַּלֹּתָֽם

verses.restored: All prophets prophesied thus, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed, for YHWH will give it into hand of king.

familiar.text: And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramothgilead, and prosper: for the LORD shall deliver it into the king’s hand.

modern.text: And all the prophets were prophesying the same, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king.” Micaiah Prophesies against Ahab (2 Chronicles 18:12–27)

original.text: וְכָל הַנְּבִאִ֔ים נִבְּאִ֥ים כֵּ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר עֲלֵ֞ה רָמֹ֤ת גִּלְעָד֙ וְהַצְלַ֔ח וְנָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him: Look, words of prophets are good to king with one mouth. Please let your word be like word of one of them, and speak good.

familiar.text: And the messenger that was gone to call Micaiah spake unto him, saying, Behold now, the words of the prophets declare good unto the king with one mouth: let thy word, I pray thee, be like the word of one of them, and speak that which is good.

modern.text: Then the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah instructed him, “Behold now, with one accord the words of the prophets are favorable to the king. So please let your words be like theirs, and speak favorably.”

original.text: וְהַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ אֲשֶׁר הָלַ֣ךְ לִקְרֹ֣א מִיכָ֗יְהוּ דִּבֶּ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּה נָ֞א דִּבְרֵ֧י הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים פֶּֽה אֶחָ֥ד ט֖וֹב אֶל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ יְהִֽי נָ֣א דבריך כִּדְבַ֛ר אַחַ֥ד מֵהֶ֖ם וְדִבַּ֥רְתָּ טּֽוֹב

verses.restored: Micaiah said, As YHWH lives, what YHWH says to me, that I shall speak.

familiar.text: And Micaiah said, As the LORD liveth, what the LORD saith unto me, that will I speak.

modern.text: But Micaiah said, “As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak whatever the LORD tells me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִיכָ֑יְהוּ חַי יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֠י אֶת אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר

verses.restored: He came to king, and king said to him, Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or refrain? He said, Go up and succeed; YHWH will give it into hand of king.

familiar.text: So he came to the king. And the king said unto him, Micaiah, shall we go against Ramothgilead to battle, or shall we forbear? And he answered him, Go, and prosper: for the LORD shall deliver it into the hand of the king.

modern.text: When Micaiah arrived, the king asked him, “Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” “Go up and triumph,” Micaiah replied, “for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”

original.text: וַיָּבוֹא֮ אֶל הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֵלָ֗יו מִיכָ֨יְהוּ֙ הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם נֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ עֲלֵ֣ה וְהַצְלַ֔ח וְנָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: The king said to him, How many times must I make you swear that you speak to me only truth in name of YHWH?

familiar.text: And the king said unto him, How many times shall I adjure thee that thou tell me nothing but that which is true in the name of the LORD?

modern.text: But the king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear not to tell me anything but the truth in the name of the LORD?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַד כַּמֶּ֥ה פְעָמִ֖ים אֲנִ֣י מַשְׁבִּעֶ֑ךָ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא תְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י רַק אֱמֶ֖ת בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: He said, I saw all Israel scattered upon mountains like sheep with no shepherd. YHWH said, These have no master; let each return to his house in peace.

familiar.text: And he said, I saw all Israel scattered upon the hills, as sheep that have not a shepherd: and the LORD said, These have no master: let them return every man to his house in peace.

modern.text: So Micaiah declared: “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, ‘These people have no master; let each one return home in peace.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְפֹצִ֣ים אֶל הֶהָרִ֔ים כַּצֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין לָהֶ֖ם רֹעֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לֹֽא אֲדֹנִ֣ים לָאֵ֔לֶּה יָשׁ֥וּבוּ אִישׁ לְבֵית֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: King of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not say he would not prophesy good concerning me, only evil?

familiar.text: And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee that he would prophesy no good concerning me, but evil?

modern.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he never prophesies good for me, but only bad?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט הֲלוֹא֙ אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֵלֶ֔יךָ לֽוֹא יִתְנַבֵּ֥א עָלַ֛י ט֖וֹב כִּ֥י אִם רָֽע

verses.restored: Micaiah said, Therefore hear word of YHWH: I saw YHWH sitting upon throne, and all army of heavens standing by YHWH, on right and left.

familiar.text: And he said, Hear thou therefore the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.

modern.text: Micaiah continued, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing by Him on His right and on His left.

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָכֵ֖ן שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֑ה רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת יְהוָה֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב עַל כִּסְא֔וֹ וְכָל צְבָ֤א הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עָלָ֔יו מִימִינ֖וֹ וּמִשְּׂמֹאלֽוֹ

verses.restored: YHWH said, Who will entice Ahab so he goes up and falls at Ramoth-gilead? One said this, and another said that.

familiar.text: And the LORD said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramothgilead? And one said on this manner, and another said on that manner.

modern.text: And the LORD said, ‘Who will entice Ahab to march up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ And one suggested this, and another that.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה מִ֤י יְפַתֶּה֙ אֶת אַחְאָ֔ב וְיַ֕עַל וְיִפֹּ֖ל בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר זֶה֙ בְּכֹ֔ה וְזֶ֥ה אֹמֵ֖ר בְּכֹֽה

verses.restored: A spirit came out, stood before YHWH, and said, I will entice him.

familiar.text: And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the LORD, and said, I will persuade him.

modern.text: Then a spirit came forward, stood before the LORD, and said, ‘I will entice him.’ ‘By what means?’ asked the LORD.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א הָר֗וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲנִ֣י אֲפַתֶּ֑נּוּ

verses.restored: YHWH said, By what? He said, I will go out and become a lying spirit in mouth of all his prophets. YHWH said, You shall entice and also prevail; go out and do so.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto him, Wherewith? And he said, I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.

modern.text: And he replied, ‘I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ ‘You will surely entice him and prevail,’ said the LORD. ‘Go and do it.’

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו בַּמָּֽה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵצֵא֙ וְהָיִ֨יתִי֙ ר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י כָּל נְבִיאָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תְּפַתֶּה֙ וְגַם תּוּכָ֔ל צֵ֖א וַעֲשֵׂה כֵֽן

verses.restored: Now look, YHWH placed a lying spirit in mouth of all these prophets of yours, and YHWH spoke evil concerning you.

familiar.text: Now therefore, behold, the LORD hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the LORD hath spoken evil concerning thee.

modern.text: So you see, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours, and the LORD has pronounced disaster against you.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י כָּל נְבִיאֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה וַֽיהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ רָעָֽה

verses.restored: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near, struck Micaiah upon cheek, and said, Which way did spirit of YHWH pass from me to speak to you?

translation_notes: Four hundred prophets speak with one voice in a royal public setting, while the messenger pressures Micaiah to conform. Consensus under patronage and threat is not reliable discernment by itself.
Micaiah's first answer appears sarcastic, and Ahab recognizes it. Prophetic speech may include irony, but vulnerable audiences need clarity rather than manipulative ambiguity.

The heavenly council and lying-spirit vision presents the Divine authorizing deception. This is a major theological difficulty and must not justify lying, entrapment, false prophecy, or claiming that misinformation is sacred strategy.
Zedekiah strikes Micaiah, and Ahab imprisons him on reduced food and water. Assault and detention of a dissenting prophet expose how regimes manage unwelcome truth.
Ahab disguises himself while asking Jehoshaphat to remain visibly royal, shifting battlefield risk onto his ally. Religious alliance does not excuse deception.
The unnamed archer shoots without knowing the target. Ahab's death is not the archer's moral triumph, and ordinary soldiers are not mere instruments of prophecy.
Ahab is kept upright in the chariot while bleeding until evening. The scene is prolonged bodily suffering, not a satisfying spectacle.
Dogs licking blood and the washing scene should not become sexualized contempt toward sex workers or bathers; the Hebrew detail is textually uncertain.
Verse 46 again uses qadesh and must not be weaponized against LGBTQ people.
Jehoshaphat's failed Ophir fleet reflects royal gold ambition, maritime labor risk, and ecological extraction. Broken ships are not proof that every failed venture is Divine judgment.
Ahaziah's conduct is linked to both parents, but Jezebel must not become the gendered container for dynastic responsibility.
safety_note: Protect dissenters from pressure, assault, imprisonment, and starvation. Do not use the lying-spirit vision to justify deception, prophetic manipulation, or certainty that opposing voices are divinely deluded. Do not weaponize qadesh against LGBTQ people or turn Ahab's death into revenge entertainment.
